reference.title: Public API and AI assistants
reference.shortdesc: Read the docs from your own tools, and let scripts and AI assistants propose changes as pull requests, with API keys that read exactly what their audience may see.

section.title: API keys
section.p: Staff create keys in the admin console under API & AI, or with POST /admin/api/api-keys; see . A key looks like opd_prefix_secret and is shown once. Only a hash of the secret is stored. Send it as Authorization: Bearer opd_….

ul.li: Scopes, which say what it can do: read (the published docs), write (read the source, validate, save changes and open pull requests), publish (also merge them when the repository's rules allow) and builds (see and start builds). publish includes write, and both include read.
An expiry (30, 90 or 365 days, or never). Revoking a key in the console or with DELETE /admin/api/api-keys/:id takes effect at once.

section.p: Each key may make 300 requests a minute; more get 429 with Retry-After.

section.title: Routes
section.p: The base path is /api/v1. GET /api/v1/openapi.json describes every route in OpenAPI 3.1 and needs no key.

strow.stentry: The calling key: name, scopes, audience, expiry.
Live release lines the key can read, and its default one.
The navigation tree: titles, topic ids, URLs.
Every topic the key can read: id, title, short description, URL.
One topic. format is markdown (default), html or text. Links point at the docs site.
Full-text search, best first; limit 1 to 50.
The docs source on the published branch, or with ref=working on the key's working branch.
Validates {"files": [{"path", "content"}]} laid over the working branch, without saving. Returns the diagnostics.
The key's working branch, its pull request and what still blocks merging.
Saves files as one commit to the key's working branch. Optional message, and expectSha to refuse the save if the file changed since it was read.
Opens, or updates, one pull request for the working branch. With {"merge": true} and the publish scope, merges it when the branch's review rules allow.
Recent builds; build the release refs now, or one ref.

section.p: Staff keys may add version (a release line such as 2) to the read routes. Org and public keys read their own line; asking for another gets 403.

section.title: How changes work
section.p: Writes use the web editor's workflow; see . Each key is an author of its own: its commits are credited to key name (API key), on its own working branch. The published branch is merged in after each save, never rebased. Publishing opens one pull request, which your branch protection and reviewers govern like any other. Files must be .dita, .ditamap or .bookmap inside the docs folder. Malformed XML is refused, and validation errors stop publishing.
On repositories that require signed commits, keys cannot save: the app cannot sign as a person. See .

section.title: AI assistants
section.p: On managed hosting, the API & AI page shows an MCP (Model Context Protocol) address for your site. Add it as a custom connector in an AI assistant such as Claude, and paste an API key when it asks. The assistant can then search and read the docs as the key's audience, and, with write, propose changes as pull requests. Self-hosted sites can point any MCP or OpenAPI client at /api/v1.
